title: Restriction transport at a geometric point: coefficient normalization and derived naturality
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Let $g:s\to s$ be any scheme automorphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], not necessarily one over $k_0$. Use the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and inverse image $G=g^{-1}$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. For $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ or $\mathcal O_E$, use the finite constant or completed coefficient sheaf $\Lambda_s$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and the structure isomorphism $c_\Lambda:G\Lambda_s\to\Lambda_s$ [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. The action on $GM$ is transported by $c_\Lambda^{-1}$.

Write $U=(s\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}s)$ and $V=(s\xrightarrow g s)$. For a sheaf $M$ of $\Lambda_s$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], let $\operatorname{ins}_{g,M}:M(V)\to(GM)(U)$ be the coprojection at $(V,(\mathrm{id},\mathrm{id}):U\to u_g(V))$ into the inverse-image colimit of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], followed by sheafification. Define $\sigma^g_M=\operatorname{ins}_{g,M}\operatorname{res}_g:M(U)\to(GM)(U)$. Under the natural evaluation identification $(GM)(U)\cong M(V)$ of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image], $\operatorname{ins}_{g,M}$ is the identity, so $\sigma^g_M$ identifies with restriction along $g:V\to U$. For a constant section $b\in\Lambda$ one has $\sigma^g_{\Lambda_s}(b)=c_\Lambda^{-1}(b)$, and $\sigma^g_M(bx)=c_\Lambda^{-1}(b)\sigma^g_M(x)$.

Termwise on any unbounded complex $N$, these maps form a $\Lambda$-linear chain map $\sigma^g_N:\Gamma(s,N)\to\Gamma(s,GN)$, natural in chain maps. Here both module actions use constant sections and the target uses $c_\Lambda^{-1}$. For every derived morphism $v:N\to N'$ in $D(s_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the induced maps satisfy $\Gamma(s,Gv)\sigma^g_N=\sigma^g_{N'}\Gamma(s,v)$; thus they define a natural transformation on the entire derived category. The sections functor is that of [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]; no constructibility, boundedness or derived-completeness hypothesis on $N$ is imposed.
